query: What if we upgrade minimist from 1.2.5 to 1.2.8? Does that resolve the issue you identified?
answer:
Target:   npm:minimist · minimist@1.2.5, 1.2.6, 1.2.7, 1.2.8 · checked 2026-11-21
Decision: 🔴 Do not adopt

Yes. Moving from 1.2.5 to 1.2.8 resolves the critical prototype pollution flaw (CVE-2021-44906),
which was fixed in 1.2.6. The databases list no other issues for 1.2.6 to 1.2.8, and licence and
maintenance were not checked.

Why
 🔴 Security: Version 1.2.5 has a critical known vulnerability (GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h /
   CVE-2021-44906). Upgrade to 1.2.6, 0.2.4 or later. (CRA Art. 13(5))
   • Version 1.2.5 has a critical vulnerability (GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h / CVE-2021-44906); fixed in
     1.2.6, 0.2.4.
     "Prototype Pollution in minimist" → https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h ✔
   • Version 1.2.5 has a critical known flaw (prototype pollution, where an attacker can change the
     behaviour of your program's objects). It is fixed from 1.2.6 on, so 1.2.8 resolves it.
     "Prototype Pollution in minimist" → https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h ✔
   🔴 1.2.5: critical vulnerability GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h / CVE-2021-44906; fixed in 1.2.6, 0.2.4
   🟢 1.2.6: no known advisory
   🟢 1.2.7: no known advisory
   🟢 1.2.8: no known advisory

What to do next
 1. Upgrade minimist to 1.2.8 (or at least 1.2.6) everywhere it is used.
 2. Check your lockfile for other copies of minimist pulled in by other packages, since some may
   still be on 1.2.5 or older.
 3. Re-run your dependency audit after the upgrade to confirm no older copies remain.

Limitations
 • Licence not checked: the question was only about the upgrade
 • Open question: Do other packages in your project depend on their own, older copy of minimist?

Not checked: maintenance, privacy, skills
